sensor: One process simulates 4 customers with 10 agents each
Agents alternate work and idle, 30 s each on average
Low load: about 10 events/s, 0.5 percent of them suspicious
With SENSOR_SEED set, the sequence repeats, event ids included
events-q: Detector replicas share it; each message goes to one of them
Bursts and detector downtime become backlog, not lost events
Sensor, detector and triage declare it identically at startup
dlq: Gets events the detector cannot parse or that lack an id
No service consumes it; dev.ps1 clean empties it
detector: Rules: secret read, pipe to shell, unknown domain, exfiltration
A synthetic 5 ms per event caps one replica near 174 events/s
On a Redis or PostgreSQL failure the event waits, never skipped
Its pod name is stored with each finding as the detector id
redis: Per agent: a sorted set of secret reads, one of web requests
Requests live only 60 s, enough to cover replica reordering
No persistence: after a restart, earlier reads are forgotten
keda: Rate: one replica per 140 events/s, 0.8 of the measured 174
Backlog: one replica per 100 ready messages, unacked not counted
The count follows whichever trigger asks for more
Scale-in waits for a minute of lower load
mgmt: RabbitMQ's management plugin, not code in this repository
Rates are broker samples, read as zero before the first one
On the host, localhost:15672 also serves the management UI
postgres: Holds findings only; events are never stored
Detector and triage set up the table at startup, under a lock
One exfiltration raised by both its events is stored once
No volume in the cluster: findings go when the pod is replaced
api: Two stateless replicas; filters bind into one static query
Health checks the database only; a broker outage fails /stats
Creates no table: queries fail until detector or triage has run
console: Polls stats, findings and customers; the next poll is the retry
Chart: 5 min of queue depth and detector count, kept in the page
A failed poll leaves the last stats up, dimmed, with the reason
Polling goes on in a hidden tab, so the chart keeps filling
browser: Filters findings by severity, customer and rule
Opens a row for the verdict text and an exfiltration's evidence
A cross-replica mark shows two detectors handled the pair
triage-q: Absorbs the rate gap between rules and a slow, rate-limited LLM
No dead-letter queue: triage drops requests it cannot parse
triage: TRIAGE_PROVIDER picks mock or gemini; dev.ps1 triage switches it
A failed call gets one retry after 10 s, then no verdict
A missing verdict never overwrites one already written
Best effort: a lost verdict is acceptable, a stuck queue is not
mock: Lets the pipeline run without a Gemini key or quota
Also chosen when TRIAGE_PROVIDER is unset and no key is present
gemini: Must answer JSON: malicious or benign, with a one-line reason
Pinned model id, not an alias; GEMINI_MODEL overrides it

publish-events: Each tool call is one persistent JSON message
No publisher confirms; a failed publish stops the sensor
consume-events: A crash before the ack means redelivery, never loss
Failed events go back about 1 s after they were taken
dead-letter: The broker routes it, by the queue's dead-letter arguments
store-finding: ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING: no second finding, no second triage
Also the detector id and, for exfiltration, JSONB evidence
shared-state: Written before read: concurrent replicas cannot both miss
1 s timeouts, no client retries; a failure requeues the event
scale-detector: Owns the replica count; a redeploy does not reset it
A new replica consumes at once: no state to hand over
read-broker: Guest credentials; full service name, from KEDA's namespace
read-stats: One request per call for the events queue, 2 s timeout
Failure: a 503 with a fixed text, never the credentials
read-findings: Newest first by id: 50 rows by default, at most 500
Also the distinct customer ids for the customer filter
call-api: nginx strips the prefix: /api/findings arrives as /findings
Same origin as the page, so the API needs no CORS headers
open-console: LoadBalancer Service: Docker Desktop maps it to localhost
The page is revalidated on load, so new builds show at once
request-triage: New findings only: id, event, rule, severity and detail
Not atomic with the insert: a crash may leave it pending
consume-triage: Manual acks; a failed provider call is retried once
write-outcome: triaged_at is set too: pending ends even without a verdict
Failed writes are requeued, unless the provider failed twice
judge-mock: In-process call; the finding is recorded as handled by mock
judge-gemini: Key sent in a header, never in the URL; 30 s timeout
Any non-200 status, 429 included, counts as a failure
